REASON: Required for material cuneiform records but not every representation domain
Physical/visible instance or component must remain separable from composed/recognized form
Configuration/realization must remain separable from mark instance unit identity and value
System-recognized functional unit differs from component count and contextual value
Cuneiform requires sign identity; modern controls use orthographic-unit terminology
Context-dependent assigned reading/pronunciation/function cannot merge with form or unit
Grammatical feature remains distinct within GRB but is not a universal representation layer
Common superclass adds no precision and risks collapsing feature value and meaning
Constrains mappings rather than forming an object layer
Records how claims are supported rather than what the represented object is
